nodes.label: Phosmith Badge Logo
nodes.description: 240x240 app-badge form of the brand: the same five-stream convergence mark placed on a dark rounded-rect (rx 28) with a radial-gradient field and dot grid, everything clipped to the badge. Heavily commented — the source doubles as the mark's construction spec.
nodes.rationale: Every luminosity is dialled DOWN versus logo-mark.svg (stream stops 0.72/0.78 not 0.85/0.9, halos 0.18 not 0.22, specular 0.86 not 0.9) because the dark field already supplies contrast; reusing the transparent version's values would bloom out.

nodes.label: Dark Radial Badge Field
nodes.rationale: Radial gradient #0F1622 -> #08090D with its centre pushed to cx 36% — offset to sit under the origin node at x=58/240 (24%) so the background is subtly brightest exactly where the light source is, faking a single-source lighting model rather than a flat plate.

nodes.label: Subtle Dot Grid Pattern
nodes.rationale: 18x18 userSpaceOnUse tile with one r=0.72 white dot at 6.5% opacity, painted as a second full-bleed rect over the gradient. Reads as engineering graph paper / a canvas transparency grid at full size and vanishes at favicon scale; deliberately below the threshold where it competes with the streams.

nodes.label: Rounded-Rect Glow Clip
nodes.rationale: A clipPath rect matching the badge (240x240, rx 28) wraps every stream, node and ambient halo. Source comment: 'Clip to rounded rect so glows stay contained'. Without it the oversized blur regions and the stream tails (which run to x=204 and beyond) would spill past the badge silhouette and break the icon's square footprint.

nodes.label: Parametric Bezier Node Placement
nodes.rationale: Node coordinates are not eyeballed: each is derived by evaluating the parent stream's cubic B(t) at a chosen t (0.50 for arc midpoints, 0.72/0.76 for outboard nodes), with the Bernstein coefficients and the full arithmetic written out in the comment above every circle. Guarantees nodes sit exactly ON their stream and makes the mark reproducible/re-derivable after any control-point edit; mirrored streams reuse results by symmetry about y=120.
